title: Malicious encoded PowerShell execution on WORKSTATION6 by pgustavo

Decoded command disables ScriptBlock logging and bypasses AMSI security controls
Connected to IP 10.10.10.5 which is suspicious (private address not in company network ranges)
Command downloads and runs code from internet (downloads_from_web: true, runs_downloaded_code: true)
User pgustavo is a domain user normally on WORKSTATION5, activity on WORKSTATION6 is anomalous
Follow-on processes conhost.exe and whoami.exe executed after the encoded PowerShell

recommended_actions.action: Reset credentials for user pgustavo and enforce MFA
Full forensic analysis of WORKSTATION6 for persistence mechanisms and lateral movement
Review wmiprvse.exe execution chain and restrict where possible

title: Encoded PowerShell execution via WMI with defense evasion on WORKSTATION6
summary: At 04:14:55, user pgustavo logged in network from 172.18.39.5 and simultaneously launched PowerShell via WmiPrvSE.exe with an encoded command (-enc). The decoded command reveals intent to disable Script Block Logging and AMSI, download malware from external host, and execute it. This follows a prior alert (ALERT-001) of malicious encoded PowerShell execution by the same user, indicating an attack chain.
evidence: Process chain: WmiPrvSE.exe launched powershell.exe with -enc flag as pgustavo on WORKSTATION6

Decoded command shows: disables_script_block_logging=true, bypasses_amsi_antivirus_scan=true, downloads_from_web=true, runs_downloaded_code=true, contains_nested_base64=true, uses_proxy_credentials=true
Command contacted URL http://10.10.10.5 for downloaded code
Multiple successful network logins from 172.18.39.5 for pgustavo at exact alert time
User pgustavo is a Domain user (lab) with normal host WORKSTATION5, not WORKSTATION6
IP 172.18.39.5 rated as internal but attack originated from unusual host for this user
related_to_prior: ALERT-001: Same user pgustavo executed malicious encoded PowerShell; this alert shows continuation of attack chain with WMI delivery and additional defense evasion

recommended_actions.action: Block IOC URL http://10.10.10.5 at perimeter
Review all recent activity on WORKSTATION6 for additional compromise indicators
Enforce MFA and review privileged account usage across lab environment

title: Encoded PowerShell C2 Beacon from WORKSTATION6 to External IP
summary: User pgustavo (normally on WORKSTATION5) executed encoded PowerShell via WMI parent process, which connected to external IP 10.10.10.5:80. The decoded command disables script block logging and AMSI, downloads and runs code from the web — classic C2 beacon behavior. This is the third alert in a coordinated attack chain (ALERT-001 → ALERT-002 → ALERT-003).
evidence: powershell.exe started with -enc flag by WmiPrvSE.exe parent process at 04:14:55
decoded command disables script block logging and AMSI, downloads from web, uses nested base64
IP 10.10.10.5 flagged as suspicious — private address not in company network ranges
pgustavo normally operates from WORKSTATION5, not WORKSTATION6
whoami.exe also launched by powershell confirming reconnaissance
attack chain: ALERT-001 (encoded PS) → ALERT-002 (encoded PS via WMI) → ALERT-003 (C2 beacon)
related_to_prior: Continuation of attack chain: ALERT-001 (malicious encoded PS) and ALERT-002 (encoded PS via WMI with defense evasion) on same host, same user. This alert shows the C2 communication phase of the same intrusion.

recommended_actions.action: Block outbound traffic to 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy
Reset credentials for pgustavo account and audit for lateral movement
Full forensic analysis of WORKSTATION6 for persistence mechanisms
Review other hosts for similar encoded PowerShell execution from pgustavo
